title: Company SonarQube Platform Defaults
source: Company SonarQube server configuration — platform-default quality gate (documented defaults).
purpose: Platform-specific defaults so the skill talks to the company server with the right project key, the right scope, and the right expectations. Read this instead of assuming a generic SonarQube setup.

server.note: Used when neither --url nor SONARQUBE_URL is provided. An explicit value always wins, so the skill still works against any other server or SonarCloud.
server.authNote: This server has authentication disabled — SONARQUBE_TOKEN is optional. Do not fail when it is unset.

edition.name: Community Build
edition.implication: Only the default branch (main/master) is analysed. Querying a pullRequest or a non-default branch scope returns nothing useful, so the skill MUST force default-branch scope on this server and say why. There is no PR decoration to wait for.
edition.consequenceForDevelopers: A feature branch gets NO gate feedback from the server. Running this skill locally before merging is the only way to find out what main will say — treat it as a pre-merge step, not just a post-failure one.
edition.upgradePath: Native PR decoration and branch analysis require a paid edition.

projectKey.appNameSource: The platform application id — normally the repository name. Derive it from the git remote's repo name, else the working-tree directory name.
projectKey.precedence: On the platform server, acme:<app> is tried FIRST. An explicit --project always wins, and a sonar-project.properties sonar.projectKey in the repo wins over the derived value because the pipeline would have used it. Off-platform, the existing detection chain (sonar-project.properties -> pom.xml -> package.json -> directory name) is unchanged.
projectKey.registeredBy: The platform at onboarding. Missing project -> ask the platform team to register it.

qualityGate.name: platform-default
qualityGate.cannotBeWeakened: Application users cannot modify quality profiles or gates; platform admins own global policy. Never advise disabling sonar-enabled or loosening a condition to get a build out.

conditions.meaning: Maintainability must be A or B
Reliability must be A or B
Security must be A or B

qualityGate.thresholdAuthority: These are the platform defaults, recorded so the skill can explain and pre-check them offline. The SERVER's own gate definition is still authoritative at runtime — report the thresholds the API returns, and only fall back to these when the API cannot be reached.

pipelineEffect.analysisStage: The CI pipeline's Sonar analysis runs on push to the default branch when sonar-enabled=true (default), before the image build
pipelineEffect.gateFailure: A failed gate can stop the CI pipeline before the image build, while a soft staging mode (SONAR_QG_SOFT_STAGING) can allow a staging image with recommendations. Inspect the actual pipeline run before declaring the staging outcome.
pipelineEffect.productionGate: Production promotion requires Quality Gate OK regardless of staging soft-gate behavior.

fixGuidance.order: Fix vulnerabilities before bugs when both appear, then coverage, then duplication, then the ratings (platform best practice).

byCondition.bugs: Open the fetched findings or the Sonar UI; fix, or refute a false positive with a justified code change — never by muting the rule
byCondition.vulnerabilities: Patch the vulnerable pattern, upgrade the unsafe API, add validation
byCondition.coverage: Add unit/integration tests for critical paths, and make sure CI actually produces the coverage report — a missing report reads as low coverage
byCondition.duplicated_lines_density: Extract shared modules; delete dead copies
byCondition.sqale_rating: Reduce code smells; simplify complex methods
byCondition.security_rating: Close security hotspots and fix vulnerabilities

antiPatterns: Disabling sonar-enabled to get a build out
Writing assertion-free tests to lift coverage
Muting or downgrading a rule instead of fixing the finding
